subject: Network separation assertion and evidence for SIG review
messages:
From: Jamie Park <jamie.park@veridian-health.com>
To: alex_martinez@redwood.ai
Cc: sig-audit@thirdpartyaudit.com
Date: 2027-04-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: network separation assertion + evidence for SIG/CAIQ review

Alex —

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. As part of our SIG/CAIQ intake we need a concise package that explains how Redwood separates customer tenancy for Dedicated and Private deployments, plus a short assertion we can include in our evidence bundle. Specifically we're looking for:

- A one-page assertion about tenant isolation guarantees for Dedicated vs Private
- Network zone mapping and traffic flow diagram (egress points called out)
- A short runbook or playbook that describes how to validate isolation (commands/tests)
- Any short-lived evidence snapshots (egress ACLs, routing table export)

Can you send a single ZIP or share a link by EOD Pacific? If there are any controls that are in progress (eg additional egress policing), call them out.

Cheers,
Jamie Park
Senior Security Engineer, Veridian Health
jamie.park@veridian-health.com

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Jamie Park <jamie.park@veridian-health.com>
Cc: sig-audit@thirdpartyaudit.com, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-05T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: network separation assertion + evidence for SIG/CAIQ review

Jamie —

Appreciate the clear list. I'm attaching a ZIP containing: a 1-page separation assertion, a PNG traffic-zone map, a short runbook (commands and checks), and an egress snapshot. Key notes up front:

- Dedicated: strict tenant fencing at the hyperplane with per-tenant VPCs and enforced egress via NAT gateways under customer-controlled routing; we publish the runbook steps to reproduce routing exports.
- Private: deployments are customer-managed VPCs (private control plane option) with our agents running in the customer's subnets; we provide the same validation checks but note that network policy enforcement surface is shared responsibility documented in the runbook.
- Ongoing: we have a planned egress-policing enhancement (FW rule automation) scheduled for Q3 2027; flagged in the assertion and runbook.

Attachments included: redwood-segmentation-runbook-v1.pdf; network-zone-mapping-20270405.png; egress-policy-snapshot-20270405.txt

Sharing link as well: https://drive.redwood.example.com/drive/u/0/folders/1a2B3cSEGMENTATION

If you want a short cover statement signed by our security lead, I can route it for signature.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
(alex.martinez@redwood.ai)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: alex.martinez@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-05T13:20:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Request: network separation assertion + evidence for SIG/CAIQ review

Alex — forwarding Jamie's ask and your draft attachments. Quick operational checklist before we send the signed assertion: 

- Confirm runbook commands are non-sensitive (no private keys or long-lived creds). If there are scripts, sanitize outputs.
- Verify the egress snapshot contains only rule identifiers and CIDR blocks (we should strip internal BGP neighbor IPs).
- Karthik: can you confirm the statement about the hyperplane fencing for Dedicated? The auditor may press on where the enforcement boundary lives (host vs overlay).

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jamie Park <jamie.park@veridian-health.com>, SIG-Audit <sig-audit@thirdpartyaudit.com>
Date: 2027-04-05T16:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Network separation assertion and evidence for SIG review

Jamie / team —

Thanks for the patience. I've reviewed the runbook and the assertion; summarized responses below and attached a redline in the ZIP. High-level bullet answers for the auditor: 

- Enforcement boundary: for Redwood Dedicated the tenant isolation boundary is implemented at the hypervisor network namespace and VPC peer boundary; we enforce per-tenant macvlan + eBPF ACLs in the host dataplane and validate via the runbook tests.
- Private deployments: when customers choose Redwood Private with customer-managed VPC, we provide the agent and a validation suite; network enforcement (route table and infra ACLs) is the customer's responsibility, documented in the "customer responsibilities" section.
- Validation primitives: runbook includes tcpdump+filter examples, control-plane logs query (time-window export), and a small Python nettest that verifies in-segment reachability is blocked.
- Evidence snapshot: the egress-policy-snapshot file includes rule ids, destinations, and timestamps — sanitized to remove internal peer IPs.

I'll sign the one-page assertion and Marissa will upload the signed PDF once I finish. If the auditor needs packet captures, we'll provide redacted captures with only header metadata.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Platform Security, Redwood Inference
(karthik.iyer@redwood.ai)

Attachments referenced: redwood-segmentation-runbook-v1.pdf; network-zone-mapping-20270405.png; egress-policy-snapshot-20270405.txt
